question: Why does the repeated fixture instantiation and teardown cycle in test_package_fixture_complex impact performance when scaling to hundreds of package-scoped fixtures with autouse dependencies?
answer: Package-scoped fixtures are finalized and re-created at every package boundary, so with hundreds of them the setup/teardown work multiplies as (number of packages) × (number of package-scoped fixtures) instead of being amortized once per session. At each package transition pytest must run every fixture's finalizer through the SetupState teardown stack and then re-execute each factory function, none of which is cached across scope boundaries. Autouse dependencies compound this: every test item's fixture closure must include the autouse fixtures and their transitive package-scoped dependencies, so pytest recomputes and re-verifies these closures per test during setup, walks the full dependency chain for resolution, and re-instantiates the chain once per package. The net effect is heavy finalizer-stack push/pop churn, repeated dependency-resolution and closure-computation overhead, and increased object allocation/GC pressure that scales linearly with packages and tests rather than remaining constant.
